label: sd-turbo-512-1step/image

provenance.summary: SD-Turbo UNet + one Euler step + TAESD decoder, emitted as ONE WebNN MLGraph in NHWC. Latent in, RGBA-packed int32 pixels out. Hand-built and tuned over four measurement passes on Apple M5 Pro / macOS 26.6.2 / Chrome 152 / Core ML backend.

source.precision: float16 throughout, no fp32 casts except the RGBA pack's 1x1 conv

recordedFrom.label: image-pass4
recordedFrom.note: The recorder captures the exact MLGraphBuilder call sequence with the shapes the backend itself inferred, so the recipe cannot silently disagree with the graph that was measured.

folds.name: euler-step-in-graph
folds.what: The single Euler step is two ops inside the graph: latent = latent_raw + (-sigma_0) * unet_out, with sigma_0 = 14.614646911621094 baked as a float16 constant (-14.6171875).
folds.why: One dispatch from latent to pixels; no readback between UNet and decoder.
folds.exact: exact in real arithmetic; the constant is the fp16 rounding of -sigma_0

folds.name: taesd-in-graph
folds.what: The TAESD decoder is appended to the same graph, so the [1,64,64,4] latent never leaves the device.
folds.delta: folding Euler + TAESD into the UNet graph gave one dispatch, latent to pixels, at 67.5 ms (pass one)

folds.name: rgba32-pack
folds.what: Core ML graph outputs are restricted to float32/float16/int32 (uint8 cannot leave a Core ML graph). So each RGBA pixel leaves as ONE int32: R + 256*G + 65536*B - 2^24, whose low bits are R | G<<8 | B<<16 | 0xFF000000. conv_out's *2-1 becomes *255; then clamp(0,255), roundEven, cast to float32, a 1x1 float32 conv with filter [1,256,65536] and bias -2^24, cast to int32. The conv is float32 because 65536 exceeds float16's 65504.
folds.delta: -6.15/-6.45 ms new prompt, -6.85/-6.4 ms cached (interleaved A/B, two blocks)
folds.mechanism: readback 3.3 -> 0.3 ms, JS conversion 1.0 -> 0 ms, and the image-graph dispatch itself 65.45 -> 62.05 ms: writing a [1,512,512] int32 output costs ~2 ms less than [1,512,512,3] float16.
folds.quality: max RGBA byte diff 1 vs the float16 path; alpha 255 everywhere

folds.name: subpixel-upsample-unet
folds.what: The three UNet Upsample2D sites (nearest 2x then 3x3 conv) are rewritten as four sub-kernels (1x1, 1x2, 2x1, 2x2) applied to the low-resolution input, then depth-to-space spelled as a transpose-free reshape (concat columns, then rows). Chrome 152's MLGraphBuilder has no depthToSpace/pixelShuffle and rejects rank 6.
folds.delta: -1.1 / -1.6 / -1.7 / -2.4 ms across four interleaved blocks; 69.48 -> 67.85 ms
folds.exact: exact; fp64 check worst relative difference 3.87e-16
folds.quality: UNet max abs 3.87e-3 -> 3.41e-3 (0.57x -> 0.50x the fp16 noise floor)
folds.cost: +49 MiB of constants (the sub-kernels are stored separately)

folds.name: layernorm-ff-fold
folds.what: The 16 norm3 -> ff.net.0.proj instances have their LayerNorm gamma/beta absorbed offline into the following linear weights. Zero ops and zero bytes changed (the affine is free inside Core ML's fused layer_norm); 32 constants removed.
folds.delta: 0.00 ms; indistinguishable from the +-1.4 ms slot bias of an interleaved A/B
folds.quality: kept purely for accuracy: UNet max abs 3.41e-3 -> 2.89e-3 (0.50x -> 0.43x the fp16 floor), image PSNR 41.89 -> 44.28 dB, image max abs 7.02e-1 -> 3.20e-1

folds.name: packed-qkv-and-scale-fold
folds.what: to_q/to_k/to_v are one packed matmul followed by split(3, axis=1); the attention scale 1/sqrt(head_dim) is folded into to_q's weights rather than applied as a separate mul.
folds.delta: speed unchanged; the scale fold halved the attention error

folds.name: timestep-projection-fold
folds.what: This graph is single-timestep (t=999) by construction, so the timestep embedding is a compile-time constant and its per-ResNet projection is folded into conv1's bias.
folds.exact: exact; deletes the whole time-embedding subgraph from the runtime path

folds.name: nhwc
folds.what: The whole graph is NHWC, though Core ML declares preferredInputLayout nchw.
folds.delta: global NCHW as a control was +3.4/+2.0 ms slower
folds.why: The transformer's permute+reshape becomes a free reshape in NHWC. The loss in NCHW is the pixel-shuffle spelling, not the transposes: Core ML prices every transpose analytically at ~7.9 us/MB, and deleting all 28 MB of Blink's transposes from a ResNet block moves it <= 0.1 ms.

rewritesRejected.name: hoist cross-attention K/V into the text graph
rewritesRejected.reason: the 32 hoisted matmuls were already fully hidden by Core ML's scheduling

rewritesRejected.name: chunked softmax (2/4/8 chunks)
rewritesRejected.number: within +-1.5 ms, curve turns up at 8
rewritesRejected.reason: moves identical bytes; the softmax cost IS the bytes

rewritesRejected.name: attention without Core ML's softmax (exp + ones-column row sums)
rewritesRejected.reason: Core ML's softmax is one fused pass; the rewrite is five. It is 1 dB more accurate, so it survives as an accuracy option, not a speed one.

rewritesRejected.name: int8 weights (per-channel and blockwise-32)
rewritesRejected.number: +0 ms, first dispatch 0.2 -> 35 s, max abs 1.2e-1 vs a 1.36e-2 bar
rewritesRejected.reason: Core ML expands int8 to float16 at load: a transfer format, not a compute format

rewritesRejected.name: int4 weights (blockwise-32)
rewritesRejected.reason: stays compressed and is dequantized every inference

rewritesRejected.name: explicit compute units, deviceType npu (CPUAndNeuralEngine)
rewritesRejected.reason: the image graph is GPU-only; the ANE cannot hold it numerically

rewritesRejected.name: TAESD decoder in NCHW
rewritesRejected.reason: isolated it was 8.8 -> 6.1 ms, but its loss was the float16 output write, already removed by the RGBA pack

rewritesRejected.name: sub-pixel upsample for TAESD's three stages
rewritesRejected.number: one stage -2, one +1, net inside noise

rewritesRejected.name: skip fusion conv(concat(h,s)) -> conv_a(h) + conv_b(s)
rewritesRejected.number: net +0.33 ms; all 12 concats are 0.25 ms of the compiled plan
rewritesRejected.reason: rejected on arithmetic; 4 of 12 instances are not even exact, as GroupNorm groups straddle the concat

rewritesRejected.name: layout assignment as a min-cut over transpose bytes
rewritesRejected.reason: Core ML's transpose price is an analytic 7.9 us/MB model, not a measurement

rewritesRejected.name: stride-2 downsampler as space-to-depth
rewritesRejected.reason: the parity sub-kernels sum to exactly 9 taps, so it is FLOP- and byte-neutral: it deletes nothing

rewritesRejected.name: text encoder on the Neural Engine
rewritesRejected.number: 7.4 ms either way; embedding error 6.25e-2, 2.7x the float16 floor
rewritesRejected.reason: fails the 2x accuracy gate with no speed to trade for it

rewritesRejected.name: WebNN <-> WebGPU interop
rewritesRejected.reason: macOS exports only float16 tensors, which is mutually exclusive with the int32 RGBA output worth ~6 ms

backendFacts: Core ML fuses 45 of 1,536 ops, all sigmoid+mul -> silu. No conv+add fusion, no constant folding, no CSE, no dead-op elimination, no transpose/reshape removal, no attention pattern match. The graph you emit is the graph that runs.
Core ML's softmax is ONE fused kernel (max, exp, sum, divide in a single pass) and costs 3.1x its input matmul at every scale: pure memory traffic over the [5,4096,4096] score tensor.

MLComputePlan's cost model is analytic, not measured: every transpose is priced at 7.90 us/MB (NHWC) / 8.39 us/MB (NCHW) to three digits regardless of permutation or shape. The hardware charges nearly nothing.
MLComputePlan returns null cost for EVERY row of a model containing one unestimable op, not just that op.
averagePool2d builds and runs standalone but fails with 'Failed to get compiled graph devices' when a second image graph is resident in the same MLContext.
uint8 cannot leave a Core ML graph: graph output dtypes are float32/float16/int32 only.

Chromium has NO compiled-graph cache. compileModelAtURL runs on every build(); the .mlpackage and .mlmodelc go to a temp dir deleted when the graph is destroyed. Reloading the page pays the full ~25 s compile again.

Core ML is gated on a non-incognito profile. An off-the-record profile silently falls back to TFLite/XNNPACK on the CPU, ~50x slower. Tell them apart with opSupportLimits(): nchw + rank max 5 is Core ML, nhwc + rank max 8 is TFLite.
Native Core ML on the identical graph runs 62.5 ms against Chrome's 62 ms: the browser adds no overhead.
Blink's own transform pipeline inserts 318 layout transposes on the NHWC path, folds 102 into constants and eliminates 85.

compiledPlan.arithmetic: 678 GFLOPs at ~12 TFLOP/s against a measured float16 vector peak near 13

provenance.floor: ~60 ms for this image graph on this backend. conv and matmul are at hardware efficiency; the five 64x64 softmaxes cannot be spelled cheaper at WebNN level because Chromium exposes no fused attention op, so the [5,4096,4096] scores are materialised; and every cheap category has been measured, not modelled, at approximately zero. Getting under 60 needs a scaledDotProductAttention op in the WebNN surface (measured natively at -15.5 ms and MORE accurate) or fewer FLOPs, not another graph rewrite.
provenance.knownDifferenceFromTheTimedRun: This recipe was recorded with latentOutput=true, so it declares TWO graph outputs: `out` (int32 [1,512,512], the image) and `latent` (float16 [1,64,64,4], the post-Euler latent, a debug output). The 67.85 ms default configuration binds only `out`. WebNN requires every declared output to be bound at dispatch, so a loader must allocate `latent` too; at 32 KB its cost is negligible, but it is a real difference between this recipe and the timed graph.

note: ops[] is the exact MLGraphBuilder call sequence. Operand names share one namespace (graph inputs keep their own names, constants k<N>, op results v<N>). Multi-output ops (split) carry `outputs`/`outputShapes` arrays as well as `output`/`outputShape`; every name in `outputs` is defined by that op.
